title: Component Orientation + Side-by-Side API Labs for tokens/buttons/tables/charts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a set of orientation guides and interactive side-by-side API labs that teach engineers and product designers how to use tokens, buttons, tables, and charts in real product contexts. The deliverables are: 1) compact usage orientation pages (do/don't + quick checklists) for each component family, 2) side-by-side API playgrounds that show component props, token overrides, and accessibility knobs, 3) migration checklist for teams moving from legacy token names and deprecated button variants, and 4) a small sample app that demonstrates composition patterns (table with chart preview + interactive row actions) to validate edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Four orientation pages published under Components > Orientation each with a do/don't checklist and two short examples; 2) API playground embedded on each component doc showing live prop toggles + generated code snippet; 3) migration note section with a legacy-to-new token mapping table and recommended shims; 4) sample app deployed to staging with a readme and linked GitHub PR; 5) at least two design reviews and one engineering review signed off.

notes: Migration guidance will include a small migration script snippet and a recommended flag for console to show legacy token shim warnings. The API playground generates code for React + plain HTML usage and will surface accessibility props (aria-*). We'll measure success via reduced 'token mismatch' tickets and time-to-first-success metric in onboarding funnel.
next_steps: 1) Complete tables and charts example data (owner: Data Tools), 2) Finish accessibility fixes for table row actions (owner: Marcus Lee / ENG-40122), 3) Final copy edit and signoff, 4) Merge PR and publish to docsite, 5) Announce in #design-system and include migration checklist in release notes.
implementation_constraints: Playground iframes must be sandboxed and lazy-loaded. Avoid adding large third-party charting libs to the docsite bundle; use a lightweight preview renderer or snapshot images for complex chart examples. Token mapping table should not rely on runtime transforms — provide explicit CSS/SCSS/JS snippets.
decision_log: 2026-02-21: Chose Storybook Controls + iframe playground approach to balance interactivity and docsite performance. 2026-03-05: Decided to lazy-load playgrounds and keep default examples minimal to reduce noise.
fallback_plan: If the interactive playground proves too heavy for docsite, fall back to pre-rendered GIFs for behaviors and keep code snippets editable via a JSFiddle/CodeSandbox link.
outcome_metrics: Targets: reduce token-related support tickets by 40% in Q2, onboarding time (first component implemented) reduced from 3 days to 1.5 days for new teams, and playground usage metrics captured via telemetry clicks to 'Copy code' and 'Run example'.
